data.cultural_impact: The name Veeranna, derived from the Sanskrit words 'veera,' which means 'brave,' and 'anna,' which means 'older brother,' signifies a fearless and courageous warrior in Hindu culture. In ancient India, such warriors or Kshatriyas were revered for their bravery and valor on the battlefield. They were not only protectors of their kingdoms but also upholders of the societal order. The name Veeranna continues to be celebrated as a tribute to these valiant warriors and their unwavering commitment to defending honor and tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: Apart from being a significant name rooted in Hindu history and tradition, Veeranna is also a name imbued with spiritual meaning. The absence of fear, which is embodied in the name Veeranna, is considered a virtuous quality in Hindu spiritual practices. Having no fear represents spiritual growth and inner strength—qualities that help guide an individual on the journey towards enlightenment. The name Veeranna serves as a reminder to continually overcome fear, embrace courage, and remain true to one's values and beliefs in life.

historical_references.reference: Veeranna, a commander in the army of the Vijayanagara Empire, was a key figure in the Battle of Talikota (1565) which resulted in the fall of the empire.
